chunks: And the Commander of the Faithful, عليه السلام, said:

"I guaranteed al-Jannah for six: a man who went out with charity and died, then for him is al-Jannah; a man who went out visiting a sick person and died, then for him is al-Jannah; a man who went out as a mujāhid in the way of Allah and died, then for him is al-Jannah; a man who went out as a pilgrim and died, then for him is al-Jannah; a man who went out to al-Jumu'ah and died, then for him is al-Jannah; and a man who went out in the funeral of a Muslim man and died, then for him is al-Jannah."

key_terms.الْجَنَّةُ: Paradise, the promised reward repeatedly mentioned for each of the six cases
key_terms.بِصَدَقَةٍ: With charity; going out to give charitable wealth for Allah's sake
key_terms.جِنَازَةِ: A funeral procession for a deceased Muslim
key_terms.مَرِيضًا: A sick person; the one being visited out of care and compassion
key_terms.مُجَاهِدًا: One striving in the way of Allah

ai.seo_question: Which deeds does Imam Ali عليه السلام mention as guaranteeing al-Jannah if a person dies while going out to perform them?
ai.summary: This hadith from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام promises al-Jannah to six kinds of people who die while setting out for righteous acts. It highlights the immense merit of charity, visiting the sick, jihad, hajj, attending Jumu'ah, and accompanying the funeral of a Muslim, showing that sincere movement toward obedience and service is greatly rewarded by Allah.
